title: Finance wants to scrap salary advances completely. Am I wrong to push back?
where: PeopleWorks Kenya community board > Compensation & Benefits

messages.author: Brenda_Atieno
messages.body:
Morning all. I'm HR lead at a mid-size food processing firm in Athi River, about 210 staff, mostly line workers on the lower pay grades. We have always given salary advances informally: someone comes to my office, explains, and if their supervisor agrees we pay them part of their salary early through payroll. No real policy, no limit written anywhere.

Our new Finance Manager wants to stop it entirely from January. His view is that we are not a bank, it messes up the cash flow forecast, and some people are taking an advance literally every month. He has a point on the last one, I won't lie.

My worry is that if we stop, people won't stop needing money. They will just go elsewhere and it will come back to us in other ways. But I can't put numbers on that and he can. Has anyone been through this? Did you scrap advances, keep them, formalise them? I have a meeting with him and the MD on the 18th and I'd like to go in with more than a feeling.

messages.author: Kiprono.HRBP
messages.body: We formalised ours two years ago, it was the best compromise. Cap it, put it in writing, make it once a month max. Finance stopped complaining once they could see a ceiling. Can't share our policy doc unfortunately, it's internal, but the bones of it are not complicated.

messages.author: Mutua_Peter
messages.body:
I'll be the dissenting voice. I ran payroll for nine years before moving into HR and I'm with your Finance guy. Advances teach people to live on next month's money. You end up with staff who are permanently one month behind and HR becomes the lender of first resort. When someone leaves owing you, good luck recovering it.

There are SACCOs for this. There are banks. Even the mobile loan apps, as bad as they are, are the employee's own decision and their own contract. The company shouldn't be in that business. Every hour you spend approving advances is an hour you're not spending on actual HR work.

My advice: give staff three months' notice, point them to the SACCO, do a financial literacy session, and close the window. It's painful for one or two pay cycles and then people adjust. They always do.

messages.author: Brenda_Atieno
messages.body: Thanks both. Peter, that's more or less exactly what Finance will say in the meeting, so it's useful to hear it put so clearly. Anyone who has actually tried closing the window, how did it go?
